results.title: Square-zero radical algebra isomorphism with varying semisimple top
results.question: Classify polynomial-bit-time isomorphism for associative algebras whose radical squares to zero while semisimple factors and bimodule multiplicities are unbounded.
results.result: Graph-isomorphism equivalence. Deterministic over each fixed finite field and Las Vegas with variable field.

results.title: Graded Lie algebra isomorphism with bounded homogeneous widths
results.question: Give FPT or polynomial-bit-time isomorphism for finite-field graded Lie algebras with bounded dimension of every homogeneous layer but unbounded number of layers.
results.result: Grade-preserving isomorphism is FPT in width for a fixed finite field and in width plus field bit length uniformly.

results.title: Integral torsion-module stable cancellation
results.question: For tensors over Z in explicitly presented modules, determine conditions under which ordinary tensor equivalence can be reflected after adjoining matching free summands to each factor with zero tensor coordinates.
results.result: Exact stable cancellation criterion, cancellation at torsion exponents 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6, and failure with 5-torsion.

results.title: Tensor automorphism groups over local rings
results.question: Compute succinct generators for stabilizers of tensors over Z/p^eZ in polynomial bit time on a specified large source class, including kernels of reduction mod p.
results.result: Generators and reduction kernel in polynomial bit time for the recognized split block-scalar class at fixed prime.

results.title: Universal geometric improvement from nondefective secants
results.question: For every nondefective proper Segre secant in three factors, does the degreewise equation test in Lee’s Theorem 3 yield a strict improvement over the generic border-rank bound on asymptotic rank?
results.result: The universal strict-improvement claim fails already at the rank-one Segre secant.

results.title: Unmarked Pfaffian recovery for alternating spaces
results.question: Determine a recognizable class of alternating matrix spaces whose full pseudo-isometry class can be recovered from the Pfaffian hypersurface in polynomial time, with explicit control of Pfaffian automorphisms.
results.result: Polynomial witness recovery for recognizable split symplectic block spaces with labelled scheme factors.

results.title: Matrix-space isometry with varying quadratic refinement
results.question: Classify pseudo-isometry of alternating spaces equipped with a quadratic refinement in characteristic two, including unknown output-basis changes.
results.result: TI equivalence in characteristic two with arbitrary output mixing, even with injective polarization.

results.title: Order reduction preserving stabilizer schemes
results.question: Give efficient d-to-3 tensor reductions that preserve stabilizers as algebraic group schemes up to explicitly described harmless factors, including inseparable characteristics.
results.result: Fixed-order reduction that explicitly preserves stabilizer group schemes up to described factors.

results.title: Order reduction preserving rank and orbit information
results.question: Determine whether higher-order TI can reduce to 3-TI with controlled tensor-rank blow-up strong enough to transfer bounded-rank algorithms without exponential parameter loss.
results.result: One ordinary 3-TI instance of rank polynomial in the input rank and tensor order, without rank decompositions.

results.title: An FPT algorithm in the number of repeated projective columns
results.question: Find an FPT algorithm for monomial equivalence parameterized by the number of coordinate columns outside singleton projective classes after removing zero coordinates, or prove a parameter-preserving hardness result.
results.result: Graph-isomorphism hardness already with zero repeated projective columns.

results.title: Epimorphism onto the dihedral group of order eight
results.question: Given an arbitrary finite presentation, classify the complexity of deciding whether the group surjects onto the dihedral group of order eight. Is it in P, NP-complete, or intermediate?
results.result: Epimorphism from finite presentations onto D8, and every fixed nonabelian dihedral group, is NP-complete.

results.title: Efficient sampling of epimorphisms with fixed central fibers
results.question: For a prescribed onto map G/Z(G)→H/Z(H), give a polynomial Cayley-table sampler for compatible epimorphisms when target centers have arbitrary prime-power exponent and rank.
results.result: Deterministic feasibility and expected-polynomial exact uniform sampling on the prescribed central quotient.

results.title: Counting conjugacy classes of extending actions
results.question: For an extension instance M≤G with a symmetric-group target, count extensions up to conjugation by the centralizer of the prescribed M-action without enumerating representatives individually.
results.result: Counting up to the marked action's centralizer is #P-complete, even with target S8.

results.title: Extension of multiple local actions with compatibility
results.question: For given subgroups M1 and M2 of a permutation group G, test whether compatible specified maps to S_d extend simultaneously to G in polynomial preprocessing and FPT time in d plus the number of local orbits.
results.result: Joint extension is NP-complete for a target of degree eight and one orbit per marked action.

results.title: Exact count of extensions preserving block systems
results.question: For a prescribed M-action and block system on its domain, count extensions to G preserving this block system in polynomial time for fixed block size or establish a counting hardness result.
results.result: Counting block-preserving extensions is #P-complete with one fixed eight-point block.

results.title: Witness sparsity for pseudo-isometry of alternating bimaps
results.question: Given two isomorphic alternating presentations with sparse input coordinates, find an explicit family requiring dense matrices for every simultaneous basis-change witness, or prove a universal sparsity bound after canonical compression.
results.result: Sparse alternating presentations can force quadratic witness density.

results.title: Geometric rank profiles versus group isomorphism
results.question: Determine whether two alternating tensors with identical rank-drop schemes in every finite extension and matching central support data can have different class-two group isomorphism types, with a family and dimensional bounds.
results.result: Identical rank-drop schemes over every extension can hide different class-two group types.

results.title: Minimum support of a permutation root extending a partial bijection
results.question: Given g and a fixed root exponent e≥2, find an e-th root of g preserving prescribed cycles and minimizing support among all roots in a subgroup specified by generators.
results.result: Minimum-support threshold is NP-complete for every fixed exponent at least two.

results.title: Maximal normal subgroup enumeration in output-polynomial time
results.question: Enumerate all maximal proper normal subgroups of a compact permutation group G with delay polynomial in degree and output-generator length, without expanding G.
results.result: Polynomial-delay enumeration of maximal proper normal subgroups via chief factors.

results.title: Orbit partition under a supplied quotient coset
results.question: For permutation generators G and normal K plus a coset of its quotient, determine all point pairs connected by a representative of that coset in uniform NC, including generators of the pointwise stabilizer interactions.
results.result: Uniform NC reachability and pointwise stabilizer computation for a supplied quotient coset.

results.title: Constant-depth circuit complexity of recovery from a partially displayed group table
results.question: Given a valid partial Cayley table with a unique completion, determine whether uniform polynomial-size AC⁰ circuits can recover each missing entry under a one-hole-per-row promise.
results.result: Uniform AC⁰ recovers every missing entry with one hole per Cayley-table row.

results.title: Tangent degenerations of bounded-depth branching programs
results.question: Characterize tangent vectors at generic points of fixed-depth bounded-size ABP varieties that remain representable by ABPs of comparable depth after degree-preserving projection.
results.result: Generic tangent vectors of layered ABP varieties need at most double width at the same depth.

results.title: Computing intersection of succinct invariant-test spaces
results.question: Given two polynomial-size arithmetic descriptions of invariant families for the same explicit product reductive action, compute a basis of the degree-d span of their common invariants without dense coefficient expansion.
results.result: Compute intersection bases of circuit-described spaces in bounded-error polynomial arithmetic time without dense expansion.

results.title: Newton-face closure for ROABPs without a consistent cut objective
results.question: Given an explicit width-w ROABP and an arbitrarily large-weight integer exposing normal for a Newton face, can the face polynomial be represented by a polynomial-width ROABP in the same order?
results.result: Newton faces preserve same-order ROABP width over every field, including with internal cancellations.

results.title: Optimal separator degree from TPP orbit geometry
results.question: For a supplied triple of finite TPP sets in a reductive matrix group, compute the minimum common degree of separating polynomials in time polynomial in coordinate input and output sizes.
results.result: Compute the minimum degree of matrix-entry TPP separators by incrementally building evaluation spaces.

results.title: Symmetry-preserving natural-proof separators
results.question: Can a small separator meta-polynomial be extended to a nonzero invariant separator of polynomial arithmetic size on a coefficient variety under a specified reductive group action?
results.result: A degree-one separator can exist even if no invariant polynomial separates its marked point from the closed set.

results.title: PIT over finitely generated transcendental extensions
results.question: For a fixed positive transcendence degree, compare bounded-degree rational-function-field PIT with PIT over the constant field when coefficient numerators and denominators arrive as circuits and their degrees are not bounded syntactically.
results.result: PIT with circuit-encoded rational-function constants is equivalent to unrestricted-degree PIT over the constant field.

results.title: Field-sensitive proof search under amortized extension degree
results.question: Can Boolean IPS certificates found over extensions of one fixed prime field be descended in time quasi-linear in their full input-plus-output bit size when the extension degree is supplied as part of the input?
results.result: Finite-field IPS descent costs quasi-linear size in the certificate gate count times the extension degree.

results.title: Geometric IPS thresholds under bounded variable incidence
results.question: Determine whether bounded-arity Boolean CSPs of bounded incidence treewidth always admit polynomial-size Geometric IPS proofs over Q when unsatisfiable, without supplying a certificate with exponential-degree denominator cancellation.
results.result: Bounded-incidence-treewidth Boolean CSPs have polynomial-size division-free Geometric IPS certificates.

results.title: Polynomial-query GI after subquadratic representation-sensitive preprocessing
results.question: In the isomorphic-priors model, determine whether polynomial-size preprocessing of a dense arbitrary n-vertex graph permits o(n^2) queries when the query is given by adjacency-access oracle and can differ by an arbitrary vertex permutation.
results.result: Quadratic adjacency-access query bound persists even with unlimited preprocessing.

results.title: Cycle indices of bilinear-forms graphs over extension fields
results.question: Compute the exact automorphism cycle index as a list of signatures with multiplicities in time polynomial in the raw graph order for all bilinear-forms graphs over finite fields.
results.result: Polynomial explicit cycle index for diameter at least two. Diameter one can have superpolynomial output.

results.title: Affine actions over finite fields from unlabeled orbits
results.question: Determine the minimum number of independent seed orbits needed to recover a finite affine group action up to abstract isomorphism when the field and ambient dimension are given and the action is faithful.
results.result: Unlabeled affine orbits give no seed bound except in the trivial and two-point cases.

results.title: Polyhedrality of quantum fractional automorphisms
results.question: Determine whether the state-evaluation set QP(A) is a polytope for every finite graph, or construct a finite graph for which it is not.
results.result: A quantum fractional automorphism set is polyhedral exactly when it is the classical automorphism convex hull.

results.title: Transport of quantum fractional automorphism sets
results.question: Determine whether a quantum graph isomorphism induces a canonical correspondence between the two QP(A) sets, compatible with their commutant descriptions.
results.result: Connected quantum-isomorphic graphs can have quantum fractional automorphism sets with different affine types.

results.title: Quantum-isomorphism invariance of quantum polyhedrality
results.question: Determine whether quantum-isomorphic graphs have polyhedral QP(A) simultaneously, even without classical isomorphism.
results.result: Quantum graph isomorphism does not preserve polyhedrality.

results.title: Quantum automorphisms of the complete directed hypergraph
results.question: Compute the quantum automorphism group of (V,P(V) times P(V)) with source and target maps, and determine whether its inclusion in S_V^+ is proper.
results.result: The quantum automorphism group of the complete directed hypergraph is the classical symmetric group.

results.title: Classical-graph realization of hypergraph quantum groups
results.question: Determine whether every quantum automorphism group of a finite directed hypergraph is the Bichon or Banica quantum automorphism group of some finite ordinary graph.
results.result: Every finite directed hypergraph quantum automorphism group has a Banica graph realization.
